title: Measuring the acidification of the phagosomal lumen in live C. elegans embryos
protocol: Use a microwave oven to melt the 4% agarose solution.
Dispense between 100–300 μL of the melted agarose solution to the center of a slide.
Immediately flatten the agarose drop by placing another glass slide perpendicular to the one holding the drop and press gently.
Let it stand for 2 min for the agar to solidify completely.
Carefully separate the two slides by sliding one against the other.
Cut the agar pad into an approximately 12 × 12 mm square using a glass slide as a blade.
Place 3 μL of M9 buffer at the center of the agar pad.
Collect between 50-80 embryos with a worm pick under a microscope and transfer them into the drop of M9 in the agarose pad.
Squeeze a thin line of high vacuum grease around the agarose pad.
Place a cover slip over the grease and press the corners first, then remaining grease to seal the slide with a P10 pipette tip.
Transfer embryos from a mixed staged worm plate to the agar pad while minimizing bacterial transfer.
Monitor the acidification process of phagosomes in developing embryos.
Identify C1, C2, and C3 cells on the ventral surface of the embryo using Phis-72 his-72::gfp::mCherry reporter.
Determine the 0 min time point by identifying the "bottom-like" structure under DIC optics.
Measure mCherry and GFP signal intensities at the center of the phagosome.
Calculate the acidification index as the ratio of GFP/mCherry signals compared to the T0 value.
Set up microscope parameters under a 20× objective.
Identify embryos carrying the fluorescent reporter (GFP+ and mCherry+) and in mid-embryonic developmental stage.
Under the 100× objective, identify embryos between 320-330 min post-1st cleavage.
Observe distinct morphological features for ventral and dorsal sides identification.
Highlight ventral hypodermal cells in purple.
Highlight dorsal hypodermal cells in purple.
Position the embryos with their ventral side facing the microscope objectives.
Define the Z-position where the z-section recording should start.
Record serial z-sections from the embryo’s ventral surface, proceeding towards the center of the embryo.
Capture 12–16 sections of 0.5 μm Z-interval for each embryo.
Start recording when the embryo reaches 320 min post-1st embryonic cell division.
